occurrences.en: This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid, but an average guy, up against the best trained, best equipped, fiercest, most brutal enemies seen in centuries.
occurrences.zh: 这不是一名志愿兵，也不是一个收入优厚的职业军人，而只是一个普通人，却要面对数百年来训练最严格、装备最好、最凶悍、最残酷的一批敌人。

occurrences.en: The United States has never had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe. G.I. Joe had a distinguished career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops.
occurrences.zh: 美国历史上从未有叫Joe的总统、副总统或国务卿。G.I. Joe有过一段显赫的军旅生涯，与德国、日本和朝鲜军队作战。

occurrences.en: He appears as a character, or a collection of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe, based on the last days of war correspondent Ernie Pyle.
occurrences.zh: 他以一个角色——或者说一组美国人格的集合——出现在1945年的电影《G.I. Joe的故事》中，该片取材自战地记者厄尼·派尔生命最后阶段的经历。

occurrences.en: Some of the soldiers Pyle interviewed portrayed themselves in the film.
occurrences.zh: 派尔采访过的一些士兵还在电影中扮演了自己。

occurrences.en: School districts across the country, most recently Los Angeles Unified, are revising their thinking on this educational ritual.
occurrences.zh: 美国各地学区都在重新思考这一教育惯例，最近的例子是洛杉矶联合学区。

occurrences.en: Unfortunately, L.A. Unified has produced an inflexible policy which mandates that with the exception of some advanced courses, homework may no longer count for more than 10% of a student’s academic grade.
occurrences.zh: 遗憾的是，该学区制定了一项过于僵硬的政策：除少数高级课程外，家庭作业在学生学业成绩中的占比不得超过10%。

occurrences.meaning: a. 不屈曲的；不屈挠的
occurrences.en: Unfortunately, L.A. Unified has produced an inflexible policy which mandates that with the exception of some advanced courses, homework may no longer count for more than 10% of a student’s academic grade.
occurrences.zh: 遗憾的是，该学区制定了一项过于僵硬的政策：除少数高级课程外，家庭作业在学生学业成绩中的占比不得超过10%。

occurrences.meaning: t. 使贫穷；耗尽...的力气
occurrences.en: This rule is meant to address the difficulty that students from impoverished or chaotic homes might have in completing their homework.
occurrences.zh: 这项规定原本是为了解决这样一个困难——来自贫困或家庭生活混乱环境的学生，可能难以完成作业。

occurrences.en: But the policy is unclear and contradictory.
occurrences.zh: 然而，这项政策本身含糊而矛盾。

occurrences.en: But if the district is essentially giving a pass to students who do not do their homework because of complicated family lives, it is going riskily close to the implication that standards need to be lowered for poor children.
occurrences.zh: 但如果学区因为一些学生家庭情况复杂、没有完成作业，就事实上对他们“放行”，那就危险地接近这样一种暗示：对贫困儿童，标准就应该降低。

occurrences.en: District administrators say that homework will still be a part of schooling; teachers are allowed to assign as much of it as they want.
occurrences.zh: 学区管理者说，家庭作业仍然是学校教育的一部分，教师想布置多少都可以。

occurrences.en: Yet rather than empowering teachers to find what works best for their students, the policy imposes a flat, across-the-board rule.
occurrences.zh: 然而，这项政策不是赋予教师权力，让他们针对自己的学生寻找最有效的方法，而是强行施加一条一刀切的规定。

occurrences.meaning: a. 全面的；在固定时间内播送的
occurrences.en: Yet rather than empowering teachers to find what works best for their students, the policy imposes a flat, across-the-board rule.
occurrences.zh: 然而，这项政策不是赋予教师权力，让他们针对自己的学生寻找最有效的方法，而是强行施加一条一刀切的规定。

occurrences.en: If the district finds homework to be unimportant to its students’ academic achievement, it should move to reduce or eliminate the assignments, not make them count for almost nothing.
occurrences.zh: 如果学区认为作业对学生的学业成就并不重要，就应该减少甚至取消作业，而不是让它几乎不计分；

occurrences.en: If the district finds homework to be unimportant to its students’ academic achievement, it should move to reduce or eliminate the assignments, not make them count for almost nothing.
occurrences.zh: 如果学区认为作业对学生的学业成就并不重要，就应该减少甚至取消作业，而不是让它几乎不计分；

occurrences.en: Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion of the grade.
occurrences.zh: 反过来，如果作业确实重要，就应该在成绩中占有显著比例。

occurrences.en: Meanwhile, this policy does nothing to ensure that the homework students receive is meaningful or appropriate to their age and the subject, or that teachers are not assigning more than they are willing to review and correct.
occurrences.zh: 此外，这项政策也无法确保学生收到的作业真正有意义、适合其年龄和学科，也无法保证教师不会布置超过自己愿意批改和反馈能力的作业。

occurrences.meaning: a. 着迷的；无法摆脱的
occurrences.en: Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls’ lives.
occurrences.zh: “粉红真漂亮”：成年的女性并不记得自己小时候曾如此迷恋这种颜色，可如今粉红色却几乎充斥着小女孩的生活。

occurrences.en: It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls’ identity to appearance.
occurrences.zh: 问题并不是粉红色本身有什么不好，而是它只是彩虹中极小的一部分；它也许以某种方式赞美了女孩时代，却又不断而坚定地把女孩的身份与外表绑在一起。

occurrences.en: What’s more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses.
occurrences.zh: 更何况，当时男孩和女孩穿的都是被视为性别中性的裙装。

occurrences.en: Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity.
occurrences.zh: 蓝色由于让人联想到圣母玛利亚、忠贞与信仰，反而象征女性气质。

occurrences.en: It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children’s marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.
occurrences.zh: 直到20世纪80年代中期，放大年龄和性别差异成为儿童营销的主导策略，粉红色才真正“属于”女孩：它开始显得天生就对女孩有吸引力，仿佛成为界定女性身份的一部分，至少在人生最初几个关键年份如此。

occurrences.en: I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development.
occurrences.zh: 我此前从未意识到，营销趋势竟如此深刻地支配着我们对“儿童天性”的认识，甚至影响我们对儿童心理发展的核心信念。

occurrences.zh: 我此前从未意识到，营销趋势竟如此深刻地支配着我们对“儿童天性”的认识，甚至影响我们对儿童心理发展的核心信念。

occurrences.en: Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.
occurrences.zh: 儿童消费史学者丹尼尔·库克指出，“toddler（幼儿）”其实是20世纪30年代服装制造商作为营销技巧推广开的。

occurrences.en: Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a “third stepping stone” between infant wear and older kids’ clothes.
occurrences.zh: 行业刊物建议百货商店，为了增加销售额，应在婴儿服装和大孩子服装之间人为创造“第三块踏脚石”。

occurrences.en: It was only after “toddler” became a common shoppers’ term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage.
occurrences.zh: 直到“toddler”成为购物者的常用词，它才逐渐演变为一个广泛接受的发展阶段。

occurrences.en: And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.
occurrences.zh: 而细分市场最容易的方法之一，就是放大性别差异——或者在原本不存在差异的地方发明差异。

occurrences.zh: 几十年来，企业一直能够为分离出来的DNA取得专利；到2005年，大约20%的人类基因已经被申请专利。

occurrences.zh: 企业高管顿时高度紧张。

occurrences.en: The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a “preliminary step” in a longer battle.
occurrences.zh: 行业组织美国生物技术产业组织安抚会员说，这只是漫长法律斗争中的“初步一步”。

occurrences.en: On July 29th they were relieved, at least temporarily.
occurrences.zh: 7月29日，他们至少暂时松了一口气：

occurrences.en: A federal appeals court overturned the prior decision, ruling that Myriad Genetics could indeed hold patents to two genes that help forecast a woman’s risk of breast cancer.
occurrences.zh: 一家联邦上诉法院推翻此前裁决，认定Myriad Genetics确实可以持有两个基因的专利，而这两个基因可帮助预测女性乳腺癌风险。

occurrences.zh: 但随着企业继续推进个体化医疗，法院恐怕仍会十分忙碌，

occurrences.en: Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents’ monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad’s.
occurrences.zh: 反对基因专利的人主要提出三点理由：第一，基因是自然产物，因此不应获得专利；第二，基因专利并非奖励创新，反而会压制创新；第三，专利形成的垄断会限制人们获得基因检测的机会，例如Myriad提供的检测。

occurrences.en: Last year a federal task-force urged reform for patents related to genetic tests.
occurrences.zh: 去年，一个联邦工作组敦促改革与基因检测相关的专利制度。

occurrences.en: In October the Department of Justice filed a brief in the Myriad case, arguing that an isolated DNA molecule “is no less a product of nature…than are cotton fibres that have been separated from cotton seeds.”
occurrences.zh: 10月，美国司法部在Myriad案中提交意见书，指出一段被分离出来的DNA分子“并不比从棉籽中分离出来的棉纤维更不像自然产物”。

occurrences.en: For example, it is unclear whether the sequencing of a whole genome violates the patents of individual genes within it.
occurrences.zh: 例如，对完整基因组进行测序，是否会侵犯其中单个基因的专利，目前仍不清楚。

occurrences.en: The case may yet reach the Supreme Court.
occurrences.zh: 这个案子最终仍可能进入最高法院。

occurrences.en: Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules – most are already patented or in the public domain.
occurrences.zh: 企业不太可能再大量申请人类DNA分子的专利——大多数早已被专利覆盖，或者已经进入公有领域。

occurrences.zh: 如今，企业开始研究基因如何相互作用，寻找能够用于判定疾病原因或预测药物疗效的相关关系。

occurrences.en: Companies are eager to win patents for “connecting the dots,” explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO.
occurrences.zh: BIO律师汉斯·绍尔解释说，企业非常希望为这种“把点连起来”的发现赢得专利。

occurrences.en: Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term.
occurrences.zh: 而它们能否成功，可能取决于与这一问题有关的一桩诉讼；该案由梅奥诊所提起，最高法院将在下一个审期审理。

occurrences.en: The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents.
occurrences.zh: BIO最近召开的一次大会还专门设置了课程，指导律师应对不断变化的专利法律环境，

occurrences.en: The great recession may be over, but this era of high joblessness is probably beginning.
occurrences.zh: 大衰退也许已经结束，但高失业率的时代很可能才刚刚开始。

occurrences.meaning: a. 唯物论的；唯物主义的
occurrences.en: Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others.
occurrences.zh: 许多人说，失业虽然极其痛苦，却也在某些方面让自己变得更好：他们不再那么物质主义，理财更加谨慎，也更能意识到他人的艰难。

occurrences.meaning: a. 审慎的；三思而后行的
occurrences.en: Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others.
occurrences.zh: 许多人说，失业虽然极其痛苦，却也在某些方面让自己变得更好：他们不再那么物质主义，理财更加谨慎，也更能意识到他人的艰难。

occurrences.en: In limited respects, perhaps the recession will leave society better off.
occurrences.zh: 从有限角度看，这场衰退也许会让社会在某些方面有所改善。

occurrences.en: At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending.
occurrences.zh: 至少，它让我们从“轻松致富、房子越大越好”的全国性狂热梦中惊醒，并给一个个人肆意消费的时代画上了必要的句号。

occurrences.en: In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms.
occurrences.zh: 经济史学家本杰明·弗里德曼在《经济增长的道德后果》中指出，无论在美国国内还是国外，长期的经济停滞或衰退几乎总会使社会变得更刻薄、更排外，也往往会阻止甚至逆转权利与自由的发展。

occurrences.en: In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms.

occurrences.en: Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes.
occurrences.zh: 反移民情绪通常会上升，种族和阶层之间的冲突也会加剧。

occurrences.en: Income inequality usually falls during a recession, but it has not shrunk in this one.
occurrences.zh: 经济衰退期间，收入不平等通常会下降，但这一次并没有缩小。

occurrences.en: Indeed, this period of economic weakness may reinforce class divides, and decrease opportunities to cross them – especially for young people.
occurrences.zh: 事实上，这段经济疲弱时期可能进一步强化阶层分化，并减少跨越阶层的机会，尤其对年轻人如此。

occurrences.en: The research of Till Von Wachter, the economist at Columbia University, suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind.
occurrences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学经济学家蒂尔·冯·瓦赫特的研究表明，并不是所有在经济衰退期毕业的人都会长期失去机会。名校毕业生能够比较快地追上他们在景气时期毕业本应达到的位置；真正被甩在后面的，是他们之下的大多数人。

occurrences.en: More difficult, in the moment, is discerning precisely how these lean times are affecting society’s character.
occurrences.zh: 更困难的是，在当下准确判断这些艰难岁月究竟如何改变社会性格。

occurrences.en: In many respects, the U.S. was more socially tolerant entering this recession than at any time in its history, and a variety of national polls on social conflict since then have shown mixed results.
occurrences.zh: 在很多方面，美国进入这次衰退时，比历史上任何时期都更加社会宽容；此后围绕社会冲突的多项全国民调也呈现混合结果。

occurrences.en: This could be no more than a passing literary craze, but it also points to a broader truth about how we now approach the past: less concerned with learning from our forefathers and more interested in feeling their pain.
occurrences.zh: 这可能只是一阵短暂的文学风潮，却也揭示了我们今天面对过去时的一项更广泛事实：我们越来越少想着向祖辈学习，而越来越关心去感受他们的痛苦。

occurrences.meaning: 灵感；鼓舞人心的人或物
occurrences.en: Today, we want empathy, not inspiration.
occurrences.zh: 今天，我们需要的是共情，而不是榜样式的激励。

occurrences.meaning: a. 可仿效的；可做模范的
occurrences.en: From the earliest days of the Renaissance, the writing of history meant recounting the exemplary lives of great men.
occurrences.zh: 从文艺复兴最早期开始，写历史就意味着讲述伟人的典范人生。

occurrences.en: Petrarch celebrated their greatness in conquering fortune and rising to the top.
occurrences.zh: 他赞颂这些人物战胜命运、登上顶峰的伟大。

occurrences.en: This was the biographical tradition which Niccolò Machiavelli turned on its head.
occurrences.zh: 这种传记传统后来被尼科洛·马基雅维利彻底翻转。

occurrences.en: In The Prince, he championed cunning, ruthlessness, and boldness, rather than virtue, mercy and justice, as the skills of successful leaders.
occurrences.zh: 在《君主论》中，他认为成功领袖所需要的技能是机敏、冷酷和大胆，而不是德性、仁慈与正义。

occurrences.en: Over time, the attributes of greatness shifted.
occurrences.zh: 随着时间推移，人们对“伟大”的理解也在变化。

occurrences.en: The Romantics commemorated the leading painters and authors of their day, stressing the uniqueness of the artist’s personal experience rather than public glory.
occurrences.zh: 浪漫主义者纪念当时最重要的画家和作家，强调艺术家个人经验的独特性，而不是公共荣耀。

occurrences.en: By contrast, the Victorian author Samuel Smiles wrote Self -Help as a catalogue of the worthy lives of engineers, industrialists and explorers.
occurrences.zh: 与此相反，维多利亚时代作家塞缪尔·斯迈尔斯在《自助》中罗列工程师、工业家和探险家的可敬人生。

occurrences.en: “The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble and manly character, exhibit,” wrote Smiles, “what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself.”
occurrences.zh: 他写道，这些人的人生展示了自助、耐心的目标、坚定劳动和不动摇的正直所具有的力量，并由此形成真正高尚而坚强的品格；这些范例说明，每个人都有能力靠自己取得成就。

occurrences.en: “The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble and manly character, exhibit,” wrote Smiles, “what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself.”
occurrences.zh: 他写道，这些人的人生展示了自助、耐心的目标、坚定劳动和不动摇的正直所具有的力量，并由此形成真正高尚而坚强的品格；这些范例说明，每个人都有能力靠自己取得成就。

occurrences.en: This was all a bit bourgeois for Thomas Carlyle, who focused his biographies on the truly heroic lives of Martin Luther, Oliver Cromwell and Napoleon Bonaparte.
occurrences.zh: 对托马斯·卡莱尔而言，这一套多少显得太过资产阶级化，因此他把传记写作聚焦于马丁·路德、奥利弗·克伦威尔和拿破仑·波拿巴这些真正英雄式的人生。

occurrences.en: These epochal figures represented lives hard to imitate, but to be acknowledged as possessing higher authority than mere mortals.
occurrences.zh: 这些划时代人物的人生难以模仿，却被认为拥有高于普通凡人的权威。

occurrences.en: For them, history did nothing, it possessed no immense wealth nor waged battles: “It is man, real, living man who does all that.”
occurrences.zh: 在他们看来，历史本身不会做任何事，也不拥有巨大财富，更不会亲自发动战争；真正完成这一切的是“人，现实的、活生生的人”。

occurrences.en: For: “Men make their own history, but they do not make it just as they please; they do not make it under circumstances chosen by themselves, but under circumstances directly found, given and transmitted from the past.”
occurrences.zh: 正如那句著名的话：“人们自己创造自己的历史，但他们并不是随心所欲地创造，并不是在自己选定的条件下创造，而是在直接碰到的、既定的、从过去继承下来的条件下创造。”

occurrences.meaning: t. 使革命化；彻底改革
occurrences.en: This was the tradition which revolutionised our appreciation of the past.
occurrences.zh: 正是这一传统彻底改变了我们理解过去的方式。

occurrences.en: This was the tradition which revolutionised our appreciation of the past.
occurrences.zh: 正是这一传统彻底改变了我们理解过去的方式。

occurrences.en: In place of Thomas Carlyle, Britain nurtured Christopher Hill, EP Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm.
occurrences.zh: 英国不再只有卡莱尔，也孕育出克里斯托弗·希尔、E.P.汤普森和埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆。

occurrences.en: Whole new realms of understanding – from gender to race to cultural studies – were opened up as scholars unpicked the multiplicity of lost societies.
occurrences.zh: 随着学者拆解那些已经消失社会的复杂多样性，从性别、种族到文化研究，一个又一个全新的理解领域被打开。

occurrences.en: And it transformed public history too: downstairs became just as fascinating as upstairs.
occurrences.zh: 公共历史也随之改变：楼下普通人的生活，终于和楼上精英的生活一样值得研究。

occurrences.en: These are the kind of workers that countries like Britain, Canada and Australia try to attract by using immigration rules that privilege college graduates.
occurrences.zh: 英国、加拿大、澳大利亚等国家正是希望吸引这类劳动者，因此其移民规则往往优待大学毕业生。

occurrences.en: They fear that it hurts their economies, depriving them of much-needed skilled workers who could have taught at their universities, worked in their hospitals and come up with clever new products for their factories to make.
occurrences.zh: 他们担心，这会损害本国经济，因为这些国家会失去迫切需要的高技能劳动者——这些人本可以在大学任教、在医院工作，或者为本国工厂想出聪明的新产品。
